Hardware

Best Android TV Box for IPTV in the UK

A good IPTV service can still feel frustrating on weak hardware. Menus take too long to respond, large programme guides stutter, and unstable Wi-Fi can turn live sport into a buffering loop. Google recommends at least 15 Mbps for 4K playback, but broadband speed only gets the stream to your device. The processor, memory, storage, and network connection still affect how quickly apps open, channels change, and playlists load.

11 min read•Updated 4 August 2026
6 boxes comparedSpecs and UK availabilityHonest drawbacks

This guide compares the best Android TV boxes for IPTV in the UK across premium, mid-range, and budget price levels. The comparison uses published hardware specifications, platform support, current UK availability, app compatibility, and the features that matter during everyday viewing.

Each review also explains the main drawback and the type of buyer the box suits. Honest drawbacks and a clear "buy if" recommendation make it easier to choose a box that suits your television, internet connection, and viewing habits without paying for features you will never use. Once you have picked one, our IPTV setup guide walks through installing a player on it.

Android TV vs Customised Android: The Important Distinction

Do not buy a box only because the product page says "Android." Android TV and Google TV are designed for television screens and remote controls, while customised Android boxes may behave more like tablets connected to a TV. Google certification is an important buying check. A Play Protect certified device has passed compatibility testing and can use licensed Google services such as the Play Store. Customised Android boxes may rely on their own app stores or require manual APK installation.

Real products show the difference clearly. NVIDIA Shield and MECOOL KM2 Plus offer a familiar Android TV experience, while Formuler and BuzzTV models often focus on extra storage, recording tools, ports, and their own viewing software. TiViMate is built for Android TV and remote navigation, so installation is usually easier on a certified device. A customised box may still run it, but you should confirm app support before buying.

The short version

Choose Android TV or Google TV when you want simple menus and easy app installation. Choose customised Android when extra storage, recording features, or specialist IPTV tools matter more to you.

Premium Tier: NVIDIA Shield TV Pro and Shield TV

NVIDIA launched both Shield models in 2019, but their hardware still competes with many newer Android boxes. Both use the Tegra X1+ processor and support 4K HDR, Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, Gigabit Ethernet, and AI upscaling. NVIDIA also released Shield Experience 9.2.4 in February 2026, showing unusually long software support for a streaming device.

NVIDIA Shield TV Pro: Best for Power Users

The Shield TV Pro gives you 3 GB of RAM, 16 GB of storage, two USB 3.0 ports, and a built-in Plex Media Server. You can connect external drives, store recordings, play local media, and switch between demanding apps without running out of space quickly.

AI upscaling can make lower resolution channels look cleaner on a 4K television, although the final result still depends on the original stream. It cannot add detail that was never present. UK pricing usually sits around £199. The cost makes more sense when you also plan to use Plex, external storage, gaming, or local media. For basic live television alone, a cheaper Android box may meet your needs.

NVIDIA Shield TV: Similar Performance with Fewer Extras

The standard Shield TV uses the same Tegra X1+ processor but has 2 GB of RAM and 8 GB of storage. You still get Gigabit Ethernet, Dolby Vision, AI upscaling, and a microSD slot. You lose the USB ports, extra memory, and Plex Media Server support. Everyday streaming remains close to the Pro, but the smaller storage allowance can become restrictive after installing several apps.

New stock can be difficult to find, so check the price carefully. When the standard model costs almost as much as the Pro, the extra memory, storage, and USB ports make the Pro a better purchase. Choose the Shield TV Pro when you need a flexible box for streaming, recording, local files, or gaming. Consider the standard Shield only when you find it at a clear discount.

Mid-Range Tier: Formuler Z10 Pro Max and Formuler Z8 Pro

Formuler boxes are a good fit when live television, recording, and familiar remote controls matter more than gaming or general entertainment apps. The Z10 Pro Max offers more memory and newer video support, while the older Z8 Pro is worth considering only when the price is much lower.

Formuler Z10 Pro Max: Best Dedicated IPTV Box

The Z10 Pro Max gives you 4 GB of RAM, 32 GB of storage, Gigabit Ethernet, dual band WiFi, Bluetooth 5.0, two USB ports, and a microSD slot. It supports 4K video at 60 frames per second and AV1 decoding, and has enough space for apps, programme data and recordings.

MYTVOnline2 is built into the box and feels closer to a traditional television service than a standard media player. You can pause live programmes, schedule recordings, manage favourites, use Picture in Picture, and move between channels with dedicated remote buttons.

You will need external storage for recordings. Watching one programme while recording another also depends on how many connections your provider allows. The Z10 Pro Max runs Android 10 and uses WiFi 5, so check retailer descriptions carefully. At around £150 with a UK plug, warranty, and return policy, it offers strong value for viewers who regularly use recording and programme guide features.

Formuler Z8 Pro: Best at a Lower Price

The Z8 Pro comes with 2 GB of RAM, 16 GB of storage, Gigabit Ethernet, dual band WiFi, and 4K output. It also runs MYTVOnline2, so you still get recording, timeshift, favourites, programme search, and channel management. For straightforward live viewing, the Z8 Pro remains capable. Its age becomes more noticeable when storage starts filling up or several demanding apps are running. The lower memory also gives you less room for multitasking than the Z10 Pro Max.

New UK stock can be difficult to find, and some listings may be imported, refurbished, or used. Check the condition, remote, power adapter, warranty, and return terms before paying. The Z8 Pro makes sense below £100. When the price moves close to the Z10 Pro Max, the newer model is the better purchase because it gives you twice the RAM, twice the storage, and newer video format support.

Budget Tier: MECOOL KM2 Plus and BuzzTV XRS4900

Both boxes target budget conscious buyers, but they solve different problems. The MECOOL KM2 Plus keeps everyday streaming simple, while the BuzzTV XRS4900 gives you far more storage and recording hardware. Your choice comes down to convenience against expansion.

MECOOL KM2 Plus: Best Affordable Google Certified Box

The KM2 Plus is a sensible option when you want one small box for live television, Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube. Google and Netflix certification means the major streaming apps run in their proper television versions rather than modified mobile builds. Inside, you get an Amlogic S905X4-B processor, 2 GB of RAM, 16 GB of storage, and AV1 video decoding.

The memory is enough for normal viewing, although the limited storage can fill quickly once you add several apps and allow them to build cache files. A USB 3.0 port gives you space for an external drive when needed. The Ethernet port is limited to 100 Mbps rather than Gigabit speed. That is still more than most online 4K streams require, but people who play large local files from a home server may notice the limit. Dual band WiFi 5 and Bluetooth 5.0 cover wireless connections.

A UK distributor currently shows the KM2 Plus at £64.99, reduced from £79.99, but the model is out of stock. MECOOL’s own store also marks it as sold out. It remains good value below £80, but paying a high marketplace price for old stock makes little sense when newer alternatives are available.

BuzzTV XRS4900: Best for Storage and Recording

The XRS4900 takes a very different approach. It has 4 GB of DDR4 RAM and 128 GB of internal storage, giving you eight times the storage of the KM2 Plus. You also get an Amlogic S922X six core processor, Gigabit Ethernet, two USB 3.0 ports, USB-C, optical audio, a microSD slot, and space for an internal SATA hard drive.

BuzzTV 5 includes PVR Plus, live pause, and recording tools. The internal drive bay is especially useful when you want recordings stored inside the box rather than leaving a portable drive beside the television.

Age is the main drawback. The XRS4900 runs Android 9, and reliable new UK stock is now difficult to find. An advertised price of £89.99 would be unusually low for unused stock, so check whether the unit is new, refurbished, imported, or missing its original remote and power supply before paying. Choose the KM2 Plus for a spare room or a straightforward mix of television and mainstream apps. Choose the XRS4900 when local recording, large storage, and physical connections matter more than having a newer operating system.

The BuzzTV XRS4900 suits buyers who need large internal storage, recording tools, and plenty of physical connections. Older models such as the standard Shield TV and Formuler Z8 Pro are worth considering only at a clear discount.

For most people buying mainly for live television, the Formuler Z10 Pro Max offers the strongest balance of controls, storage, and recording support. The Shield TV Pro remains the better all-round entertainment device. Keep your login details private, and follow the setup guide written for your chosen player.

Pairing Any Android Box with IPTV UK

When your IPTV UK login details arrive, start with the player that best matches your box. Installing several apps at once usually makes setup more confusing. On an NVIDIA Shield or MECOOL KM2 Plus, TiViMate is often the easiest option because it is designed for Android TV and works well with a remote. Add the M3U link or Xtream Codes details supplied with your account, then allow the channel list and programme guide to finish loading.

Formuler users can begin with MYTVOnline2, which is already installed on supported models. BuzzTV XRS4900 owners can use BuzzTV 5 for channel browsing, recording, live pause, and scheduled viewing. You only need another player when you prefer a different layout or set of controls. Our installation guide covers the Android TV steps in full, and you can check what you will be watching on the channel list.

When signed in, open one live channel and one film or episode. Close the player, open it again and verify that your account is still saved. If nothing loads, check the server address, username, password and expiry date before changing any box settings. Keep your login details to yourself and only use services authorised to provide the content you watch.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which Android TV box is the best choice in the UK for 2026?+

The Formuler Z10 Pro Max is the best fit when live television and recording are your priorities. Choose the NVIDIA Shield TV Pro when you also want gaming, Plex, local media, and external storage. The MECOOL KM2 Plus remains a good budget choice when genuine UK stock is available below £80.

Will TiViMate run on every Android box?+

TiViMate is designed for Android TV and remote control use. Installation is normally easiest through Google Play on a compatible certified box. Some customised Android devices may support manual installation, while Formuler and BuzzTV boxes already include their own television focused players.

Is the NVIDIA Shield TV Pro worth around £200?+

It is worth the price when you will use AI upscaling, Plex Media Server, USB accessories, external drives, or gaming. A cheaper device will usually offer better value when you only need one player for live television.

Does Android TV offer an advantage over customised Android?+

Android TV and Google TV usually offer easier app installation, licensed Google services, and menus designed for a remote. Customised Android boxes may provide more storage, recording tools, or specialist software, but app support and updates depend more heavily on the manufacturer.

A good box cannot compensate for an unreliable service. Test playback during busy evening hours, open the channels you normally watch, and check whether the programme guide and support meet your expectations.
